f.statement: Healthcare providers and caregivers should report any AEFI that is of concern; both minor and serious AEFI cases should be reported. This includes serious AEFIs (death, hospitalisation, persistent or significant disability or incapacity such as paralysis, or potentially life-threatening events); signals and events associated with a newly introduced vaccine; AEFIs caused by immunisation error; allergic reactions (e.g. anaphylaxis, hives, bronchospasm, oedema); seizures; any events causing significant parental/caregiver or community concern; and swelling, redness or soreness at the injection site lasting more than 3 days, or swelling extending beyond the nearest joint, or inability to move the limb.

Healthcare providers and caregivers should report any AEFI that is of concern. Both minor and
serious AEFI cases should be reported.

    ▪ Signals and events associated with a newly introduced vaccine
    ▪ AEFIs caused by immunization error
    ▪ Allergic reaction e.g. anaphylaxis, hives, bronchospasm, edema
    ▪ Seizures
    ▪ Any events causing significant parental/caregiver or community concern
    ▪ Swelling, redness, soreness at the site of injection if it lasts more than 3 days or swelling

f.title: Apply the seriousness criteria for adverse events
f.statement: Serious adverse events are those AEs that: (a) are life-threatening or fatal; (b) cause or prolong hospital admission; (c) cause persistent incapacity or disability; or (d) concern misuse or dependence. Any medical event that requires intervention to prevent one of these outcomes may also be considered serious.
